**The most contention-sensitive endpoint.** Single endpoint for both
free and paid workshops; the server branches internally on
`workshop.price`.

## Idempotency (`registration-paid.md` §Bước 2)

The `X-Idempotency-Key` **header** (UUID v4 generated by client) is
required. Lifecycle (3-state, ADR-08, ADR-15):

| Server state | What client sees |
|---|---|
| `completed` | Cached response replayed (idempotent) |
| `in_progress` (locked) | `409 request_in_progress` |
| none | Normal first-time processing |

**Client must generate the key once before the first attempt and reuse
it on any retry** — generating a new key on retry bypasses idempotency.

## Rate Limiting (`rate-limiting.md`)

This endpoint applies T2 (user: 30/60s) **and** T3 (user×workshop: 5/60s).
T1 (IP) does not apply — authenticated users are identified by `user_id`.
T3 is the critical guard: spam on one workshop doesn't penalise registering
for a different workshop.

## Free workshop flow

1. Rate limit check (T2, T3).
2. Pre-check `seatsAvailable` via Redis cache (fail-fast, no DB round-trip).
3. Claim idempotency key (`in_progress`).
4. OL retry loop (≤2 attempts, ADR-03):
   - `INSERT registration ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`.
   - If `rowsAffected=0` → student already registered → return existing.
   - `UPDATE workshops SET seatsAvailable -= 1, version += 1
      WHERE id=? AND version=? AND seatsAvailable > 0`.
   - On version mismatch → ROLLBACK and retry.
5. Mark idempotency `completed`.
6. Invalidate cache key (fire-and-forget).
7. Enqueue confirmation notification via BullMQ (async).
8. Return `201` with `qr_code`.

## Paid workshop flow

Same as free up to step 5, but `status='PENDING'` and **no QR code**.
The response `next_step` directs the client to call `POST /payments`.

Mark a scheduled session Held and give it the next number
description:
Marks a Scheduled session Held. sessionNumber becomes one more than the highest number already used in the same group, or 1 when none. Marking Held never renumbers sessions that are already Held. Undo (SCRUM-41, BR-13) is the story that renumbers later Held sessions. The response does not include who changed the status; that is stored on the row.

The session is counted into payment cycles in the same transaction (US-22, BR-06 to BR-08): once in the open cycle of every student whose enrollment covers the session's academy-local date, whether they attended or not (AC-02), and once in the open cycle of the (instructor on the session, the session's group) pair: an instructor is paid per group (ADR-0015), so it never counts in their cycles for other groups. cyclesUpdated lists those cycles with their counter after the change. When a counter reaches the plan's session count the cycle becomes due and the next one opens at 0 under the plan version in effect for it (a plan change applies from the next cycle, BR-10). A student, or an instructor for this group, with no open cycle (no plan yet) is skipped: the session is not counted for them, and marking it Held is never refused because of that. The admin sets the starting point when creating the plan. When a group changes instructor, the former instructor's cycle for the group stays in progress and takes no new session (no partial payment), and the new instructor is counted once they have a plan for the group. After the counters are written, each active admin who holds payments.manage gets one summary when a counted cycle reached 2 sessions left, 1 left, or became Due (US-27). One notification lists everyone who crossed a threshold with this session. A bug in that text does not refuse the Held mark.

The request carries what was taught (topic) and the attendance of every student of the session (SCRUM-79). Everything is written in the same transaction: Held, the number, the topic, the attendance, the cycle counters and the payment reminders. A refusal anywhere changes nothing. topic is trimmed, 1 to 300 characters, otherwise 400. attendance holds every student of the session exactly once (the students are the group's enrollments that cover the session's academy-local date, the same list as GET /sessions/{id}/attendance) and is an empty list for a session with no students. Each line has the rules of AttendanceRecord, and an optional note (trimmed, up to 500 characters, also for an absent student). The same rules apply to the admin and to the instructor.

The checks run in this order and the first problem is the one answered: the body shape (400), the session (404, 403, then 409 for its status, the clock and the order rule), the same student twice (400), a student who is not in the session (422 STUDENT_NOT_IN_SESSION), a rating on an absent student (422 STUDENT_ABSENT), and last a student of the session with no line (422 ATTENDANCE_INCOMPLETE, one field error per missing student: field attendance, message the student id).

scheduledAt must be at or before the server clock, otherwise 409 SESSION_NOT_STARTED. A session that is not Scheduled is 409 SESSION_NOT_SCHEDULED (including a second mark).

Order is per group. Scope own is 409 SESSION_OUT_OF_ORDER when another session of the group has a strictly earlier scheduledAt and is still Scheduled. Scope any (the admin) may mark Held anyway: the earlier session stays Scheduled, so it is not numbered and will not enter a payment cycle. Cancelling that missed session is SCRUM-27. Both scopes are 409 SESSION_OUT_OF_ORDER when a Held session of the group has a strictly later scheduledAt, so this session cannot take a higher number than one that happens after it. An equal scheduledAt does not block, so two sessions at the same instant (a make-up, for example) do not block each other. A later reschedule must refuse a move to before the latest Held session of the group.

Scope own may mark Held only when the instructor on the session is the caller. Being the group's current instructor is not enough. After an instructor change, an unrecorded session stays on the previous instructor, and only an admin can record it or use the unlock above.

Session report (US-29, FR-26): in the same transaction, after the attendance is recorded and the cycles are counted, every active user who holds sessions.read:any gets one notification of type session_report with the counts (present out of total), the topic cut to 60 characters, up to three absent names and the average performance rating when there is one. It opens the session details. It is sent once per session: editing the attendance or the topic, or an undo and another Held, does not send it again. A student's note is never part of it. A bug in the text does not refuse the Held mark.

Actual times (SCRUM-80): startedAt and endedAt are required, each a local wall-clock "HH:mm" in the academy's timezone (a malformed or missing one is 400). The start is on the session's academy-local date, the date of scheduledAt in that zone, so a session cannot be entered as having started the day before. The end is on the same date, or on the next date when its clock time is earlier than the start (a session across midnight). They are turned into instants with the academy's zone rules, so they are right on the days Egypt changes its clocks, and stored as actualStartedAt and actualEndedAt in the same transaction. 422 ACTUAL_TIME_INVALID on endedAt when the end is not after the start (the same time twice is not read as 24 hours), or is after the server clock, so Held with times is entered after the session ended. There is no minimum or maximum duration and no rule on lateness: the start may be before or after the planned time. Payment cycles count sessions, not minutes, so they are not affected. The admins' session report adds the duration after the attendance count.

**Authorization**: Requires admin privileges to create mappings.

**Path Patterns**: Support exact paths and parameterized paths using curly braces
(e.g., `/api/v1/users/{user_id}`, `/api/v1/groups/{group_name}/members`).

**Method Mapping**: Each combination of path pattern and HTTP method can only
be mapped to one action.

**Action Reference**: The action must exist before creating a mapping. Use the

This method updates a security group.

A security group refers to a set of rules that determine what network traffic is allowed to enter or leave a particular compute instance. It acts as a virtual firewall, controlling inbound and outbound traffic based on predefined rules.

Security groups operate based on predefined rules that allow traffic based on specified criteria, such as source IP address, destination IP address, port number, and protocol.

When editing a security group, you can add and delete the inbound and outbound rules. You can only define rules that allow traffic, not deny it. All traffic is denied except for explicitly allowed traffic.

Security groups control TCP, SCTP, GRE, ESP, AH, UDP, and ICMP protocols, or all the selected protocols at once.

After creating a security group, a set of default rules is added to the security group. These rules are immutable, and you can't edit or delete them. When editing a security group, _you should provide the default rules along with any other rules._

All traffic in the selected protocol is allowed if the IP range in a rule is set to `0.0.0.0/0`.
